correctness.rationale: The open neighborhoods are exactly Δ(A_e∪B_e). Under girth at least five, every mixed pair from A_e×B_e uniquely identifies its generating edge e: any other connector creates a triangle or square. Every mixed face is therefore confined to one generating simplex. Two explicit descending-size elementary-collapse stages reduce that simplex relative to its unmixed faces to one cross edge; the proof of freeness covers all global cofaces. The remaining graph of sphere boundaries X_v≅S^{deg(v)-2} follows the incidence graph H and has m-n+1 circles; adding one edge interval per e adds m circles. Counting degree-three boundaries yields 2m-n+1+n3 circles, with remaining higher spheres and no torsion. The package verifier independently checks all 5062 free-face collapses and mod-two homology in six graphs with 11766 augmented faces. Universal scope rests on proof, not finite data.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The object is the open Lovász neighborhood complex N(L(H)) on vertices E(H), generated by Δ((S_u\{e})∪(S_v\{e})) for e=uv. The clique complex Cl(L(H)) is the flag complex generated by S_v, and the closed Čech nerve is generated by Δ(S_u∪S_v), including center e. Both are genuinely different from the open complex. The only strongly related existing topological classification is the block-graph open-neighborhood theorem, but L(H) is not a block graph when H has a long induced cycle. The new collapse and high-degree sphere formula are absent from these inspected statements.

value.rationale: An explicit infinite-family homotopy classification for a natural graph-topology construction, with unbounded base degrees and overlapping long cycles. The unique cross-edge collapse is a structural lemma with genuine new higher-dimensional sphere contributions, not a routine consequence of the clique-complex or closed-neighborhood classification. A natural four-regular projective-plane incidence graph yields 79 circles and 26 two-spheres; a bridge-joined example additionally exhibits an S3 summand. The exact integer homotopy and torsion-free assertions answer the natural shape question, even without downstream applications.
